newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, prospects for recovery slim.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, prospects for recovery slim.

text.p: Slovenian shares slipped back on Thursday and traders said a continued stark absence of buying incentives could drive the index down towards 1,100 points over the summer.
"I think there will be no fresh information or foreign money on our market before the summer so the index could slowly fall down to 1,100 points," said Jasna Zontar, a trader at brokers Modra.
The SBI index lost 0.22 percent, or 2.96 points, to 1,315.96.
Overall nine shares fell, five rose and 14 were untraded. Turnover rose to 88.6 million tolars from 59.2 million.
Traders, who said said liquidity of the market remained low, had been pinning their hopes for a recovery on the return of foreign players. But this was looking doubtful.

"I am afraid foreign players are already losing their patience and according to my information some of them are already switching to neighbouring markets that are apparently more attractive," Zontar said.
In February, the central bank blocked foreign trading, ordering them to open custody accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 licensed banks if they wanted to trade in Slovenian shares.
Since then the index has fallen over 20 percent, while average daily volume has petered out to a fifth of its previous size.
Shopping centre operator BTC had the highest turnover, falling 1.96 percent to 14,500 tolars on volume of 1,799 shares for total turnover of 26.8 million tolars.
Traders said the fall was a reaction to Wednesday's over 5.5 rise fuelled by expectation that BTC may soon complete its global depository receipts issue.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska Bank led the day's decliners, tumbling four percent to 14,880 tolars on volume of 100 shares, also following a technical correction.
Bank Probanka was the top gainer, jumping 4.50 percent to 20,900 tolars on volume of 456 shares, for total turnover of 9.5 million tolars.
Traders attributed the rise to the bank's good business results and plans to expand its business and raise its market share.
